conversation.user: I've got 420 sq. ft. of wall at 10 inches for a backyard office. Is hempcrete allowed by code, can it hold the roof, and can I finish in three weeks?
conversation.assistant:
Based on your dimensions of 420 square feet of net wall area at 10 inches thick, your computed hemp-lime volume is approximately 9.9 cubic meters. 

Regarding your questions:
Hemp-lime construction is referenced in the 2024 International Residential Code Appendix BL, but model-code inclusion is not proof of local adoption or permit approval, so you will still need local authority and qualified-professional review. Because hemp-lime is a non-load-bearing infill, it cannot hold up the roof on its own; a conventional structural frame, commonly timber framing, must carry the roof, floor, wind, and seismic loads. Finally, for a cast-in-situ approach, natural curing before final plaster typically takes about 3 to 6 weeks depending on conditions, so finishing everything within three weeks may be tight. 

Would you like to explore using pre-cast blocks or cast-in-situ for your installation method?

canonicalFinalState.volumeBasis: 420 sq ft × (10 in / 12) × 0.0283168 = 9.91088 m³; displayed to one decimal place
